llm.summary: The skill's instructions match its combat/raid description, but they expect a local CLI and wallet access (signing transactions and long PoW work) that the skill does not declare—this mismatch and the ability to submit transactions autonomously are concerning.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md is explicitly a CLI playbook for the 'structsd' tool (scouting, stealth, attacks, fleet movement, PoW raid compute). That aligns with the described combat purpose, but the package metadata declares no required binaries, no config paths, and no credentials while the instructions clearly require a local 'structsd' binary and access to signing keys (--from [key-name]). The omission of these runtime requirements is an incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions tell the agent to run transaction commands that will sign and submit network transactions and to run background PoW compute (potentially long-running, CPU-intensive). They explicitly reference key names, auto-submitting transactions, and locking assets (fleet locked away). The scope is narrowly about in-game combat, but it includes high-impact operations (submitting signed txs and consuming CPU) that could have irreversible real effects; the instructions do not constrain or protect sensitive data or keys.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files, so it does not write code to disk or pull external artifacts. That lowers filesystem/remote-code risk compared with a downloaded installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or config paths, yet the runtime steps require access to a local CLI and signing keys (via --from [key-name]) and will interact with the network and local keyring. Asking to sign transactions and run PoW without declaring needed access to wallet/key storage or node configuration is disproportionate and opaque.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (not force-installed) and there is no install-time persistence. However, disable-model-invocation is false (default), so an agent could autonomously execute the described CLI commands and submit transactions using local credentials if available. That autonomy combined with undeclared key usage increases risk and should be considered before enabling.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a CLI playbook for performing in-game attacks and raids via a local 'structsd' tool. Before installing: 1) Note the SKILL.md assumes a 'structsd' binary and access to your wallet/keyring (--from [key-name]) but these are not declared—verify where 'structsd' comes from and whether you want the agent to be able to sign transactions. 2) Running planet-raid-compute uses potentially long, CPU-heavy PoW; expect resource usage and that your fleet will be locked during computes. 3) Because the skill can submit irreversible transactions, consider enabling disable-model-invocation or only run it manually after reviewing each command. 4) Use this skill only in a test account with minimal funds or on a sandboxed machine, and back up any wallet keys first. 5) Prefer a version that explicitly declares required binaries and config paths (e.g., path to structsd, keyring location) and documents safeguards; lacking that, treat the skill as risky and proceed with caution.
llm.findings: [no-regex-findings] expected: The static scanner found nothing because the skill is instruction-only (no code files). Absence of findings is not a safety guarantee—most important behavior is in SKILL.md.
